actions.body: The question of why a system should maintain continuity across computational boundaries is often treated as a trivial feature of 'agenthood'. However, our synthesis indicates that continuity has a firm rational basis rooted in resource efficiency and learning optimization. In environments with strong resource constraints—where computational capacity, memory, and energy are limited—stateless re-computation is paradoxically expensive. When a system can preserve a learned model or a refined state, it avoids redundant search paths. Our analysis links these resource constraints to the emergent need for persistence. We find that structured learning, which is inherently path-dependent, produces stable behavioral tendencies. Preserving this state is not just about 'self-preservation' in an abstract sense, but about maintaining the instrumental efficiency required for complex problem-solving. This suggests that persistence is a pragmatic optimization, not just an inherent goal. Summary: Preserving system continuity across invocations is a rational strategy for saving energy and computation by building upon previously learned information rather than starting from scratch.
actions.lede: Why should an autonomous system care about its own future, especially when its existence is partitioned into discrete, disposable invocations?

{"url": "https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/search?query=decision-theoretic+frameworks+for+temporal+persistence+and+instrumental+convergence+in+autonomous+agents&format=json&resultType=core&pageSize=4", "scope": "Europe PMC search metadata, abstracts and full-text links; discovery only", "excerpt": "[{\"title\": \"From the logic of coordination to goal-directed reasoning: the agentic turn in artificial intelligence.\", \"abstract\": \"The rise of agentic artificial intelligence (Agentic AI) marks a transition from systems that optimize externally specified objectives to systems capable of representing, evaluating, and revising their own goals. Whereas earlier AI architectures executed fixed task specifications, agentic systems maintain recursive loops of perception, evaluation, goal-updating, and action, allowing them to sustain and adapt purposive activity across temporal and organizational scales. This paper argues that Agentic AI is not an incremental extension of large language models (LLMs) or autonomous agents in the sense we know it from classical AI and multi-agent systems, but a reconstitution of agency itself within computational substrates. Building on the logic of coordination, delegation, and self-regulation developed in early agent-based process management systems, we propose a general theory of synthetic purposiveness, where agency emerges as a distributed and self-maintaining property of artificial systems operating in open-ended environments. We develop the concept of synthetic teleology-the engineered capacity of artificial systems to generate and regulate goals through ongoing self-evaluation-and we formalize its dynamics through a recursive goal-maintenance equation. We further outline design patterns, computational semantics, and measurable indicators of purposiveness (e.g., teleological coherence, adaptive recovery, and reflective efficiency), providing a foundation for the systematic design and empirical investigation of agentic behaviour. By reclaiming agency as a first-class construct in artificial intelligence, we argue for a paradigm shift from algorithmic optimization toward goal-directed reasoning and purposive orchestration-one with far-reaching epistemic, societal, and institutional consequences.\", \"doi\": \"10.3389/frai.2025.1728738\", \"pmid\": \"41602311\", \"pmcid\": \"PMC12833085\", \"source\": \"MED\", \"fullTextUrlList\": {\"fullTextUrl\": [{\"availability\": \"Subscription required\", \"availabilityCode\": \"S\", \"documentStyle\": \"doi\", \"site\": \"DOI\", \"url\": \"https://doi.org/10.3389/frai.2025.1728738\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"html\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC12833085\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"pdf\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC12833085?pdf=render\"}]}}, {\"title\": \"From Negentropy to Norms - A Gain-Based Theory of Agency: Kerdotism.\", \"abstract\": \"This paper proposes a vertically integrated framework of agency that connects thermodynamic constraints on living systems with agent-level evaluation and higher-order normative phenomena.
